mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the Federal Funds rate above 5.25% in the month preceding the forecast period is associated with a negative 20-day S&P 500 forward return due to higher discount rates eroding expected equity payoffs.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 5.25% in the month prior
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive or flat during the identified Fed rate hike episode, with p-value > 0.05 in a two-tailed test versus pre-hike period.

mechanism_narrative: When monthly UNRATE falls below 4%, labor market slack increases, reducing expected wage growth and depressing S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive and statistically significant (p < 0.05) during periods of low unemployment, contradicting the mechanism.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in HOUST (household spending index) of at least 2% followed by a positive 60-day S&P 500 forward return indicates that stronger consumer demand anticipates future corporate earnings growth.
candidate_trigger: HOUST increases by ≥2% in the current month
failure_condition: No significant correlation (p > 0.1) between HOUST momentum and 60-day forward returns in subsequent months.

mechanism_narrative: When INDPRO (industrial production) falls for two consecutive months below its 12-month moving average, the S&P 500 20-day forward return tends to be negative due to weak economic momentum and reduced earnings expectations.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO < 12-month MA for two consecutive months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive and statistically significant during such dual-month INDPRO declines.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous declines in both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL (inflation) over the prior 3 months predict a positive 5-day S&P 500 forward return as the market anticipates rate stabilization and lower inflation pressure.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL both decline over the previous 3 months
regime_hint: Dual softening of rates and inflation
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not significantly different from zero during such dual declines (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sudden spike in PAYEMS (employment) by over 10,000 in a month coincides with a positive 20-day S&P 500 forward return as the labor market absorbs excess supply, reducing recession risk.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by >10,000 in the current month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns remain negative despite the employment surge (p < 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When RSAFS (retail sales) exceeds 400 million for three consecutive months, it signals resilient consumer demand, leading to a positive 60-day S&P 500 forward return in the following quarter.
failure_condition: No significant positive return (p > 0.1) in the next quarter after the three-month streak.

mechanism_narrative: A prolonged decline in GDPC1 (GDP) by 2% or more over the last quarter is associated with a negative 20-day S&P 500 forward return as investor confidence weakens in corporate earnings prospects.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 declines by ≥2% over the last quarter
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive during such GDP declines (p < 0.05).
